document: Expand legal aid to cover cases of defamation, Legal aid is currently not available for defamation cases. This means that people, who may not have a large income, can have their reputations and lives ruined by false statements made about them, and be unable to afford recourse. The Government needs to expand legal aid to help prevent injustice., Defamation law only protects those that can afford to take legal action. However, too many people are becoming victims of false statements being made about them - particularly online where there is a wide audience. These actions can have detrimental impacts on an individual's life: from ruined reputations, job losses and mental health issues. Expanding legal aid to cover defamation cases could help protect people from defamation.

Fund Improved Diagnosis Pathways For Neurodivergence, We are asking for funding to improve diagnosis pathways for neurodivergence. 

This includes ausistic spectrum disorder (ASD), attention defeceit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), dyscalculia, dysgraphia, dyslexia, dyspraxia, tourette's syndrome, all personality disorders and more., The diagnosis pathway for any neurodivergence is essential for ensuring appropriate and effective courses of treatment in most cases.

However, the time it currently takes to get a formal diagnosis can be many months, or even several years. This lost time affects the neurodiverse population's mental health, productivity and safety.

The provision of funding for improved diagnosis pathways would be an important first step towards addressing this.

Ban isolation across schools in England, Ban the use of isolation as punishment across schools in England., Ban the use of isolation across schools in England. It's an outdated practice and should not be used on children.

The British Psychological Society has said that the use of isolation booths is not backed by evidence and has been proven not to be effective, and adds that such approaches to children’s behaviour are overly simplistic and “run counter to the understanding of child development”.

We need a complete shift in how we support our most vulnerable young people.

Increase support for men's mental health and awareness of available support, Too men of all ages are suffering from mental health issues, especially during the current cost of living crisis. The Government needs to raise awareness of the help available to men for getting mental health support, and also fund increased support for men with mental health issues., The Government should do more to raise awareness to the public of support available to those with mental health issues. There should be more posters in public and on public transports more tv ads more leaflets. By funding improved support and raising awareness of this, the Government can help ensure that people receive the support they need.

Ban loudspeaker/mechanical calls to prayer, We want the Government to stop councils from being able to give permission for places of worship to use loudspeaker/mechanical calls to prayer, which can happen at various points of the day. We believe this is noise pollution, and should not be happening in our towns and cities., Calls to prayer could also be objectionable to people who are of different faith groups including atheists, when they are enjoying their peace within their own homes/work/worship. We believe these calls infringe on individual privacy and enjoyment, yet councils, who employ abatement officers still allow loudspeaker/mechanical usage in many areas.
 
We believe allowing these calls to prayer is inconsistent with the Human Rights Act 1998, Article 8 and 9 and also legislation, "Noise & Statutory Nuisance Act 1993", "Control of Pollution Act 1974"

Make hair colour a protected characteristic to prevent discrimination, Extend discrimination protection in the Equality Act to hair colour, to try and help prevent discrimination and bullying of people for their hair colour., Some people see bullying red-haired people is acceptable, but this is prejudice against people for a trait they were born with.
 
Whilst some people might see it as a laugh to belittle, demean and abuse children for being red haired or their phenotypical characteristic, it can be very harmful stripping these children of their positive self-identity and confidence and worse it can lead to school refusal, health problems, and even self-injurious behaviour.

Reform the Gender Recognition Act 2004, Legal recognition of non-binary people, accompanied by the introduction of a Gender ‘X’ marker on legal documents (passports, driver’s licenses, etc.)., De-medicalization of the process of legally changing your gender, instead allowing self-determined change without medical proof.
 
This could help:
 
- Reduce fear and confusion during ID checks
- Reduce instances of misgendering (when other people refer to you as the incorrect gender) in institutional and professional environments
- Ensuring non-binary identities are recognised in medical contexts, helping to protect patients from discrimination and misgendering
- End legal invisibility of non-binary people
 
Showing the Government is committed to equality and protection of minorities.

#genderxuk

Require MP candidates to live in the constituency for a minimum of 5 years, We ask that prospective parliamentary candidates be required to live in the constituency they wish to represent for a minimum of 5 years, before they stand for election. We would allow for certain exceptions to this rule due to constituency boundary changes., The role of an MP is to represent the interests of constituents. Currently a candidate is able to stand for election in a constituency that they could live hundreds of miles away from or even in another (overseas) country. We believe an MP can most effectively represent a constituency if they have lived there and have a clear understanding of the needs and challenges of its residents as well as the political and economic context of that constituency.

Create a cross-party body to introduce an integrated NHS and Adult Care Service, Create a statutory cross-party body to develop and implement proposals for an integrated NHS and Adult Care Service. This new service should have funding secured on a ten year rolling basis., We believe the failure of successive governments to implement an integrated service has significantly contributed to the ongoing crisis in the NHS and social care.

Royal Commissions and Parliamentary Reports have not been followed up by adequate action by the Government.

"The historic political failure to take a long-term approach to the provision of health and adult social care has been a major stumbling block to longer-term sustainability" (Para. 334 House of Lords Select Committee Report 5.4.17)

A Royal Commission into the scientific efficacy of animal experimentation., We the undersigned demand a Royal Commission into the scientific efficacy of animal experiments & call for a transparent discussion to assess whether alternatives are adequately funded and promoted., It is increasingly clear that vivisection is outdated, costly, unethical & bad science. There has not been a proper enquiry into the use of animals in laboratories for far too long. The U.K. is falling behind other countries and losing our reputation as a leader in animal welfare due to this failure to change in line with the scientific evidence.

Review Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), We want the Government to review Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), and consider ways of improving how these are delivered. This could include the operation of a triage service, where young people with complex needs are quickly referred to specialist services., There are serious issues with the availability of mental health services for children and adolescents, with some children waiting up to two years to receive support. Referrals are being made by GPs and schools but unfortunately children are having to wait too long to get support needed. We believe a Government review could help identify ways of improving the delivery of these services, so that young people receive the support they need, when they need it.

Reduce term holidays in schools and increase summer holidays (at least 2 weeks)., School holidays are too many during the term, mid term, Christmas and Easter during School period. My request is reduce some of these holidays and increase the number of summer holidays. Summer holidays are very few when we compared with other western countries., With the short period of school holidays most of the parents and children are paying 3 times excessive amounts on summer holidays on flights and others because everyone wants to go at the same time becuse holidays are not enough during the summer. I don't see any sence of giving a week holiday for every six weeks shcool. Please consider to increase the summer holidays by decreasing other term holidays by at least 2 weeks.

Government to set a standard price for MOTs, We ask the Government to set a mandatory standard price for the MOT test so that MOT test stations cannot discount this important road safety check., The DVSA are challenged by the reliability and quality of mot tests conducted by companies that discount MOT prices. We believe there is a definite risk of poor standards created by discounted prices that can directly affect road safety.
 
The MOT test is a measure of a vehicle's standard and safety,  and as such should not be something that can be done on the cheap!

Amend the British Museum Act to allow the acceptance of repatriation requests, The return of the Rosetta stone and other artefacts to their countries of origin is a matter for the British Museum. However, in order for the British Museum to be able to accept a request for these artefacts to be repatriated the British Museum Act needs to be amended., The unlawful removal of the Rosetta stone and other artefacts has been contentious ever since they were removed from their countries of origin. The Rosetta stone represent the part of the history and cultural identity of millions of Egyptian people. The British Museum has said it “needs an act of Parliament” to repatriate them. It is time for Britain to finally cooperate.

Let’s show the world our British sense of fair play by making this gesture of goodwill and friendship.

Review how local authorities support children with special educational needs, We want the Government to review how local authorities support children with special educational needs. This should include how assessments for EHC plans are conducted, and support for children waiting to be assessed. We believe too many SEN children are not getting the support they need., In too many cases parents struggle to get local authorities to assess their child  for an EHC plan, or are unable to provide the evidence local authorities want - in part because of long waiting times to access children and young people's mental health services.
 
Every child deserves an education, but until the needs of all children are quickly and correctly identified, this will not happen. A Government review could identify failures in current practice, and measures to ensure that support for children with special educational needs is provided in a timely manner.

Condemn burning of the Holy Qur’an in Sweden, We ask our Government to publicly condemn the burning of the Qur’an incident in Sweden., Holy Qur’an was burnt in Stockholm – Sweden on 21 January 2023.

The Sweden Government allowed the protest where the Qur’an was burnt under freedom of expression, but has since condemned this act.

This sort of incident promotes Islamophobia on targets the Muslim community, and we want the Government to be clear it condemns actions like this.

Prohibit the publication of drone film of private property taken without consent, To prohibit the publication of drone footage taken on/over private property without the written consent of the property owner. This is sometimes referred to as 'auditing', and whilst many 'auditors' behave with integrity, many are provocative in order boost viewing numbers (and income)., At present the publication of drone film is not sufficiently regulated. 'Auditors' can film businesses with no consent and then publish their footage online. The drones may alarm residents, livestock and workers. The footage may, unintentionally, give viewers insights into site security, the presence of property desirable to thieves, and be used for acts preparatory to terrorism. 'Auditors' often obscure their identity, and will not give their names, which can leave businesses frightened.

Stop MPs payrises until public sector pay is addressed to an acceptable level., Do not give yourselves increases in pay without proof you are dealing with issues of the UK economy and public sector pay being at an acceptable level, Increases in MPs salaries are not acceptable at this time whilst we have nurses and teachers using foodbanks

Introduce tougher sentences for knife crime, For too long now people are getting away with light sentences when it comes to knife crime, including murder and attempted murder.
I propose that anyone caught in possession of a blade should be handed a 2 year custodial sentence.
For wounding/attempted murder - 10 years
And murder - 25 years, Knife crime appears to be on the up and not just in major cities but in towns and villages as well. It is almost as if youngsters see it as ‘trendy’ now to possess a blade.
Only through harsher sentences will they start to see sense. Suspended sentences and fines/community orders for possession of a blade aren't a big enough deterrent, and neither are the light sentences for wounding and attempted murder with a knife.
If changes aren’t made soon this is only going to get worse.

Make legal aid available for appeals against probation licence conditions, Make legal aid available for convicts to be able to appeal against license conditions., We believe the probation service has too much power and are treating many convicts unfairly, but often cannot afford to challenge the licence conditions that are set.
 
Legal aid was taken away for these types of cases, and we want it reinstated.

Increase funding for special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) education, I would like the Government to increase funding for SEND education, so that local authorities can provide more school places for children with SEND. Parents shouldn’t have to fight to get their child the education they need., I believe there is a national crisis regarding SEND school places. SEND education needs more funding so that local authorities are able to build more specialist SEND schools. There are so many families nationally with children that have no specialist SEND schools locally. This isn’t something new, This is a crisis that’s been going on for many years & there’s not enough funding in many areas. I believe that the Government need to look into this and make more funds available to help with SEND Education, so families that have children with special needs/disabilities are able to get a specialist school setting for their children they deserve without having to fight for a place.

Increase the investment limit on Premium Bonds from £50,0000 to £100,000, I am looking for the Government to increase the investment limits on NS&I Premium Bonds., This is a very widely supported product. It will encourage more money to be saved with the protection of the Government.

Uk companies adopt 'Ms' as the default when gathering personal data about women, If the Government told UK businesses that Ms must be the default when gathering personal data for women, then over time women would stop being defined by marital status. Individuals could still opt to be Miss/Mrs/Dr but by default all adult females would be Ms., All men are identified as Mr, regardless of marital status. Yet women are still defined as Mrs or Miss. The use of Ms is not widespread and therefore comes with its own connotations such as divorced, widowed, spinster etc. Companies do not need to know a woman's marital status and for as long as women are defined by this, we cannot achieve gender equality.  If Ms was the default and was adopted by the majority it would remove any stigma attached to it and reduce inequality and unconscious bias.

Reopen Billericay Police station, Help us to get the police station back open to bring the crime rate of the town down and keep people safe and secure, Help us to get the correct information on how we can achieve this.

Increase funding for adult and child social care services, Increase funding for social care services for adult and children. This could help reduce costs of prolonged hospitalisation and reduce burden on GP and specialist services, and so reduce waiting lists, Too much money is wasted with adults and children being stuck in expensive hospital beds, because of a lack of social care provision to support the vulnerable with high level of needs on discharge. This is costing the tax payer and blocking beds for other people with acute illnesses, as well as causing trauma, institutionalisation and worsening physical and mental health for patients trapped in hospital settings. Invest in social care services to support people in the community.

Introduce harsher punishments against organised human trafficking , We ask the Government to take the lead in tackling human trafficking, in particular of women and children for sexual exploitation. We ask for the Government to increase sentences for anyone involved in these crimes, to deter those operating at all levels of human trafficking networks., UN reports indicate a continued rise in the numbers of people being trafficked globally, particularly women and children. Current measures are clearly not sufficient to tackle this heinous crime which strips victims of their dignity, freedom and many of their basic human rights. The institution of harsher punishments in the UK will act both as a warning and a deterrent to those involved to break the chain of trafficking taking place on our doorsteps.

Establish border checks for hauliers in Calais to find any undocumented migrants, We want the UK Government to establish border inspections for hauliers intending to cross the British channel, to find any undocumented migrants.

If any undocumented migrants are found on the truck after it has been checked the haulier should not be liable for this., Currently hauliers can face large fines if an undocumented migrant is found once their vehicle has crossed the channel. Due to this some hauliers just let migrants go if they find them.

To avoid this we want the UK Government to take responsibility for ensuring that there are no undocumented migrants on trucks crossing the channel, by establishing secure checks. We believe the current system of CO2 checks and scans is not fit for purpose.

Launch an independent review into future health & care needs & how to meet them, There seems to be no adequate plan to address the crisis in health & social care. The Government should commission an independent review to: identify the country's future health & care needs, and, to develop costed options to meet them. This could inform the Government, Parliament and the public., The issues are complex, solutions potentially expensive. Politicians seem unable or unwilling to take the necessary action to address the future challenges. We believe a truly independent review, with appropriate input from stakeholders, offers the best chance that decisions about health and care would be made in an informed and honest way, reflect the real challenges and great opportunities of the future, and meet peoples' desires and expectations.

Change the law regarding people carrying and using knives, I want the government to change the law and the sentencing handed down to individuals who use and carry knives including much tougher sentences for carrying and a minimum life sentence for killing someone., There are far to many people mainly teenage boys carrying knives as either a gang culture thing or as protection from other teens who they see as a threat or from a rival gang. We have tonight had a sixteen year old boy stabbed to death on his way home from school with four individuals arrested soon after. It is becoming an all too familiar story lately both locally and nationally and something needs to change to try to deter this from becoming an even bigger problem than it currently is.

To make incident involving a knife to receive more severe punishments., To make knife crime punishment more severe to help with the increase in knife before it is more common and people to be more anxious about what the future could see like for the country., I feel that if something isn't done then it could get out of hand and lead to it being more common and affecting more people lives.
This would put more strain on public services because of it.

End Behaviour Hub programme and investigate impact of school behaviour policies, We want the Government to end the Behaviour Hub programme and investigate the impact of school policies such as toilet restrictions, shortened breaks, isolation, zero tolerance and SLANT on the mental health of students., We have serious concerns that punitive techniques and regimented school culture (morning addresses, silence as default, etc) may cause significant harm to children, especially SEND pupils.
 
Behaviour is important and we want schools to be calm and focussed so every student has the best chance to learn. But, we believe there are better methods to achieve this aim – particularly restorative and relational approaches.
 
Please investigate behaviour polices in schools in England and end the Behaviour Hub programme.

Impose minimum sentences for first offence of possession of a knife, We want the Government to introduce minimum sentences for possession of a knife from the first offence. These should be 4 months detention and a £1,000 fine for 16-17 year olds, and a 6 month custodial sentence and a £1,000 fine for people aged 18 and over., In 2013/14 there were just under 27,000 offences involving a knife or sharp instrument. In 2022/23 this had increased to over 45,000. There have been hundreds of thousands of these offences in the last decade.
 
We need tougher sentences that apply from the first offence. Currently minimum sentences only apply for multiple offences.
 
We need a deterrent to make people think twice before they decide to pick up the knife!

Give all shareholders a voice by bringing Company Law into the 21st Century, Help more investors engage with UK plcs by modernising the Companies Act: Give beneficial shareholders the right to direct info on plcs they invest in & plcs the right to visibility of who their shareholders are, make email a requirement to shareholding registration, & recognise digital AGMs., Outdated legislation stops shareholder voices being heard. Almost half of individual shareholders can’t directly engage with the company they invest in, as they invest via platforms, the rest are constrained by a paper-based system. At the same time, companies are losing sight of who their investors are. Digital first reform will be better for shareholders, better for business and ultimately, better for Britain – making the UK a more attractive place to invest and to list.

Improve access for Adult Autism Post Diagnostic support / Occupational Therapy, Allow all Autistic adults with a confirmed valid Diagnosis (from any NHS trust/private clinic) to access NHS autism post diagnostic support/ Occupational Therapy without restrictions. Improve online information around managing Autism and it's comorbidities (e.g. hyper/hyposensitivity, sleep, diet), My local neurodevelopmental team in Coventry said they cannot offer me post diagnostic support/OT because I didn't get my diagnosis through them, I got it privately. They said the restriction was made by the local commissioning board. I have only been sent website links, it's not enough. I'm finding it difficult to access occupational therapy via the NHS to help with my sensory issues because of this restriction. All autistic adults should be able to access occupational therapy in the NHS.

Deny holding 500 single-adult males at Portland Port on a barge for 18 months., The Home Office confirmed that the Bibby Stockholm barge will host more than 500 single-adult males in Portland, Dorset, near Weymouth. This matter has only been discussed in private with the port owners which has exacerbated the issue for the public. We demand the immediate reversal of this plan., There has been no account of the effects this could have on the many small businesses and people relying on the summer trade. Tourists, visitors and families flock to Weymouth & Portland in the summer to enjoy the lovely resort and beaches. The barge itself will, in effect, be a quasi-prison, where hundreds of young men will spend most of their time. Doing what? The port is heavily restricted and what happens if there’s trouble on board? Not to mention, what will they do in the wider community?

Add a Crown to the insignia of Junior Rates of the Royal Navy, When an organisation earns the prefix “Royal” it normally incorporates the crown of the current monarch in its insignias. This especially applies to military units. Currently the Junior Rates of the Royal Navy wear no crowns on their uniforms in any place., Being a Royal service, I believe that it does a disservice to those of the lowest rates of the Royal Navy to not be able to show this Royal status in any way, when other service people do so proudly. This is highlighted more when the Senior Rates and Officers of the Royal Navy and members of the Royal Marines do wear crowns.

Half road tax in areas where roads are not adequately maintained, Our roads need to have an inspection each year via an independent body, with road tax halved for cars registered in any area where roads are not adequately maintained., The Government needs to recognise the lack of action by local authorities to  sort out our roads. Each vehicle has to pass an MOT inspection to clarify our vehicles are fit for our roads.
 
A road inspection needs to be taken every year in every area, to ascertain if our roads are fit for our vehicles. If the roads in area are found to be maintained to less than 85% of an acceptable standard, all vehicles registered within the area should have their road tax halved until roads in that area are improved.

Review police handling of cases involving vulnerable suspects, I have seen how the police can mismanage cases involving vulnerable suspects, especially when the suspect has mental health issues, learning disabilities, autism or ADHD. I want the Government to review police handling of cases involving vulnerable suspects, and consider how this could be improved., The Government needs to ensure that vulnerable suspects, including those with mental health issues, learning disabilities, autism or ADHD, are treated fairly by the police, and are not disadvantaged by having a condition or criminalised for something which could have been averted.
 
The review could look at improving training for police officers on how to handle and communicate with vulnerable suspects, requiring the use body cameras, and how suspects can be referred to mental health services.

Do not house asylum seekers on ships with free access to the mainland, The Home Office recently confirmed a barge will accommodate hundreds of adult men in Portland, Dorset. This has not been consulted on, and has raised local concerns. We call on the Government not to house asylum seekers on ships with free access to the mainland, at least without proper consultation., We believe the Government has not adequately considered the effects this will have on the many businesses and people relying on the summer trade. Tourists, visitors and families generally flock to the coast to enjoy peaceful resorts and beaches; including, Weymouth and Portland.

Mandatory 10-year sentence for possession of a knife, We want the law to be changed so that if you found guilty of illegal possession of a knife, you receive a mandatory 10-year sentence., We believe this could help reduce knife crime.

Make school uniforms a choice not a requirement., School uniform should not be a requirement as it does not improve the child's learning or well-being in any way, if anything it decreases the child's willingness and enjoyment of being at school it also decreases creativity in a child's work., Mandatory school uniforms limit self-expression, they can create a financial burden for families, and may not be suitable for certain climates or activities. there is lack of evidence on impact on academic achievement or behaviour, and they have the potential to discriminate against cultural or religious practices. Instead, schools should prioritize creating a culture of respect, inclusivity, and self-expression that celebrates diversity and encourages students to be their authentic selves.

Create a cross-party Commission on the future governance of England, Accept the recommendation of the House of Commons Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee to “bring forward … the establishment of a Bill to create a cross-party Commission on the future governance of England that is funded by and responsible to Parliament.”, The committee’s report of 31 October 2022 sets out very clearly “the urgent need for significant reform to the way that England is governed,” identifying six main areas of concern with local government in England:

1. Too complex
2. Too opaque
3. Too centralised
4. Ineffective and wasteful funding arrangements
5. Significant geographical inequalities
6. People feel disempowered

Full report at: https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5803/cmselect/cmpubadm/463/summary.html

Introduce higher maximum sentences for possession of more dangerous knives, Introduce knife classes, so possession of knives with serrated edges or long blades can lead to longer maximum sentences than offences involving shorter knifes or knives that are not serrated. This would be a similar approach to classes for drugs., Knives are not all the same and possession of knives designed specifically to be harmful should be punished more harshly than someone carrying utility or kitchen knives. It should act as a deterrent for criminals to use more dangerous knives, as they could face longer sentences. currently the maximum sentence carries 4 year maximum sentence for any knife.

Introduce longer winter holidays for schools instead of summer, Instead of summer holiday period of 5-6 weeks these holidays should be moved to December/January, possibly increased to eight weeks, or full two months. School holidays are for bad weather., Summer months do not see as many serious illnesses among school age children as winter months of Dec-Feb.
Hospital admissions for respiratory illnesses in children has been consistently higher for winter months. This problem is exacerbated by need to send children to school most of winter, making prevention against infectious diseases difficult.  
This could have a knock on effect on their attendance and long term development.
Longer winter holidays is a much better option, which should be trialed.

Review the Special Needs Education System, This education system means autistic people and people with SEND are made to suffer alone before getting help. 

The system really is broken and not fit for purpose. 

No parent should ever have to fight for their child. 

System level reform is required to achieve real change., I want to end the suffering of autistic people and people with SEND. No parent should ever have to fight for their child and no autistic child or with SEND should have to suffer alone just because the education system stops them getting help.

Make parents accountable of children under 18 and fine them., To bring in legislation and that law that parents will be held accountable and fined for their children’s bad behaviour and criminal actions in public., With the scourge of anti social behaviour in community’s and some children under the age of 18 behaving in a feral manner with disregard for law and consequences, we need some form of deterrent that will have parents making sure their children behave better in society and fining parents should help make parents control their unruly children more so the law abiding citizens don’t suffer in community’s at the hands of feral yobs.

Require media containing edited human features include a symbol showing this, I would like to see a symbol placed on every piece of media containing human features, including newspapers, magazines, adverts and social media viewed in the UK, to show if they have been edited, including filters and photoshop., The pressure on women and men in society today, particularly young adults to 'look good' is hugely based on what we see in the media. This is leading people to believe that we should look like this when in reality many of these images have been heavily edited. Having a symbol to show when media has been edited will help with understanding that these images are not an accurate representation, and could help prevent the negative effects this can have on mental health.

Don’t allow affordability checks for sports betting, The Government should ban bookmakers from conducting affordability checks on bettors. Bettors shouldn’t have to experience intrusive checks covering aspects of their finances. The Government should also abandon its proposals for frictionless checks that they’ve included in the recent white paper.,

Replace the Sovereign Grant with a system of voluntary contributions, Replace the Sovereign Grant (£86.3m in 2021-22) with a system of voluntary contributions where members of the public can decide whether to contribute to the official expenditure of the Royal Family., The Royal family and its duties are respected by many; others are ambivalent at best. There is not unanimous support.

Support could be gauged by determining how many are prepared to pay for a service, and what value they place on it.
 
A fully-costed and transparent target budget could be set 12 months in advance, and a 'crowdfunding' appeal launched to achieve that target.
 
Tracking against target would facilitate adjustment to resources in the case of shortfall or oversubscription.
Give students a right to a day off on their birthday, Because everyone should be able to celebrate their special day with their family without restrictions and/or repercussions.,

Review arrangements for the prescription of contraceptive pills, We want the Government to review arrangements for the prescription of contraceptive pills, with a view to improving patient safety. Currently patients can easily get repeat prescriptions without seeing their GP or having any health checks. This can mean risk factors are missed., My sister passed away in April 2020 from a blood clot which we believe was caused by the contraceptive pill. She had not had a check-up for the 18 months she had been on the combined pill. If she had received regular check-ups the clot could have been caught and she might still be here today. Her name is Riszka Szymkowska and she was 22 years old.

Review the safety of Endoscopic Thoracic Sympathectomy and the aftercare., We want the Government to review the safety of Endoscopic Thoracic Sympathectomy surgery and the wellbeing of patients who have previously undergone this surgery., I and many like me were advised to have this surgery, but the adverse effects of this surgery can be truly life altering.

The procedure involves surgery on the sympathetic nerve chain and can cause an avalanche of knock-on problems to the heart, lungs, blood vessels, and severe compensatory sweating.

Some people who have undergone this procedure have become shadows of their former selves. I was not properly informed about the risks of this surgery, and would never have agreed to it, had I been.

Close the park on our estate as it is attracting anti social behaviour, We would like the park on our housing estate removed as it is attracting anti social behaviour and gangs of teenagers causing issues.,

Introduce statutory payments for Special Guardians of children, Special Guardianship, where a person is given the care of a child by the courts, is commonplace in the United Kingdom. Carers do not always receive any form of financial assistance, other than Child Benefit. A child will normally be cared for until they are 18 years old., All special guardians should receive substantial financial support. They are saving local authorities millions of pounds a year, looking after children who would otherwise be under local authority care, in care homes or in paid foster homes. The current arrangements for providing financial support to Special Guardians vary locally, and are normally means tested. Special Guardians can spend tens of thousands bringing children up, and many get nothing. Current arrangements are outdate, and should be made fair for all.

Make 12 hour shifts illegal, Suicides within the construction industry are increasing year by year. I want my government to really take action and make 12 hour shifts illegal. I myself have had to work 12 hour shifts containing abnormal shift rotations and I can tell you now that these NEED to STOP!, We believe people in this country who work 12 hour shifts have no time to exercise, spend quality time with loved ones, eat properly, have enough sleep etc. Enough is enough, this is the United Kingdom and it is time to take a stand for your construction industry. Over 500+ men and woman are taking their own lives yearly and this number continues to grow.

Urge other nations to prevent looting of British shipwrecks, The Government should urge nations where our shipwrecks lie to take more active measures to ensure to protect shipwrecks, including those that are designated war graves, and ensure anyone responsible for looting these are brought to justice., There have been recent reports of suspected looting of British Warships that are designated war graves, and I don't think enough is done to prevent this, or bring those responsible to justice. Men who died on these vessels gave their lives to defend the free world. It's only right we defend their remains.

Fund reconstructive surgery and mental health support for all FGM survivors, We want the Government to provide funding to ensure Female genital mutilation (FGM) survivors have access to reconstruction surgery and appropriate mental health support through the NHS. Many survivors struggle to receive the surgery and support they need at present., In the UK alone, it is estimated that tens of thousands of women and girls have undergone FGM or are at risk of being subjected to this practice. The physical and emotional impact of FGM is devastating. The UK Government can take a significant step forward in ensuring the wellbeing of survivors. I request the UK Government provides funding to ensure the provision of reconstruction surgery and mental health support for FGM survivors through the NHS.

Reverse the decision not to proceed with the Animal Welfare (Kept Animals) Bill, We wish for the Government to reverse its decision to scrap the Animal Welfare (Kept Animals) Bill, and to dedicate Parliamentary time to its passage and enact it into law., The Bill was introduced by the Government and was supported through its Second Reading and Committee Stage. This petition calls on the Government to reverse its decision not to proceed with this Bill, and to take it through Parliament to become law.

Fund university scholarships for minorities and disadvantaged students, We want the Government to provide funding for university scholarships for students from ethnic minorities, disabled people, low-income families, and so on, because they deserve opportunities to attend higher education without financial burdens., Data published by the Office for Students shows that 81.6% of students from the most deprived backgrounds completed their course, compared to 92.2% from the most advantaged group.
 
We must strive for 100% of students completing their courses, because every one of those pupils has a light within them that is ready to shine. We can help achieve each and every one of these desired futures with the assistance of the Government.

End means testing for Legal Aid for proceedings in the Court of Protection, Legal Aid should not be means-tested for families subject to proceedings in the Court of Protection. Why should some families pay thousands of pounds for legal advice or be expected to self represent in a complex judicial system with only the most determined persisting?, Remove means testing for Legal Aid for all families who are involved in proceedings, including those pitted against publicly funded barristers and solicitors in the Court of Protection. Remove financial barriers in the way of families at a time when important decisions about their loved ones' care are at stake, including residency, contact and capacity.

Families cannot be expected to navigate these complex systems. How is this a level playing field? Please show your support by signing this petition.

Ban physical discipline/punishment of children, I want the Government to ban the use of physical discipline/punishment by parents or carers in all cases. We believe it causes children to be scared of their parents who use it. We think some children won't speak up if the physical discipline/punishment is leaving lasting effects., We think children want to ban to the use of physical discipline/punishment because it causes damage to the relationship between the parents and the children.

Lifetime ban on dog ownership for anyone whose dog attacks a person, I want the Government to introduce a lifetime ban on dog ownership for anyone who owns a dog which attacks a person. There are too many stories of people, even children, being attacked, sometimes killed, by dogs. , I think that this will prevent attacks from happening as much. Those who are unable to properly train and control a dog should not be allowed to own one. I think this will make our streets safer and prevent further instances of dog attacks on people.

Require schools to have appropriate uniform rules for hot weather, We want schools to be required by law to have appropriate uniform rules for hot weather. Currently many children are forced to wear uncomfortable clothing to school in summer eg. blazers, heavy skirts, ties and long trousers., This is a nationwide issue, with over 9 million school children and many schools unable to afford improved ventilation, Government leadership is required. 
 
We want practical low and no cost changes to the uniform rules. In hot weather schools should be required to allow children to wear shorts and thin skirts, with no ties or blazers.
 
If children are hot, uncomfortable or dehydrated it does affect their concentration..
 
With our young people’s physical and mental health in mind we must allow them to dress appropriately for their learning environment.

Set up a Public Inquiry into age discrimination and ageism in the UK, Age discrimination and ageism are endemic in UK Society with negative stereotypes of older people providing justification for blatant discrimination across the economy. We believe the Equalities and Human Rights Commission has failed to grasp the scale of the problem and a Public Inquiry is needed., A Silver Voices Survey of 1000 over-60s found, for example, that a large majority had experienced negative ageist attitudes by the public and direct age discrimination by the finance/insurance sectors. Over half had missed out on retail special offers or services because they were unable to pay digitally. The drive by businesses and public bodies to force people to use apps to access services is accentuating the problems. A Public Inquiry should suggest ways to stamp out ageism in UK society.

Legally recognise non-binary gender, The Government needs to recognise non-binary as a legal gender. Non-binary people in the LGBTQ+ community feels silenced and invisible. We need the Government to reform the Gender Recognition Act 2004 to legally recognise non-binary as a gender and help non-binary people to feel heard, Currently non-binary people are not recognised in law. This leads to misgendering, especially in institutional organisations. Having our gender legally recognised would help us to feel so much more respected and accepted within society, in accordance with fundamental British values. Non-binary people have campaigned for years to be recognised, a change is needed. We want to be seen within society and currently we feel hushed away. Change the law so we can have our place recognised in society.

Do not issue guidance making it unsafe for school students to question gender
, According to media reports, the Government plans to publish guidance that would tell schools to ban students who wish to change their pronouns from competitive sport, and to inform parents about students questioning their gender identity., Parents would reportedly have to give consent before the student's gender identity could be respected at school, and this could be vetoed by a head deciding it'll have "mental effects" on other students, regardless of what the parents say.
 
Even under Section 28, gay students could be gay at school without fear of being outed.
 
Gender-questioning students could have transphobic parents. Or another student could claim "mental effects" as part of a bullying campaign.

This could result in direct endangerment of children.

Urgent amnesty for undocumented migrants living in the UK for 5+ years, We want the Government to take the necessary action to grant an urgent amnesty to undocumented migrants with no criminal record, who have been living in the UK for 5 or more years, enabling them to live, work, and contribute to the UK without fear or limitations., The urgent request for the Government to grant an amnesty to undocumented migrants (with no criminal records and residing in the UK for 5+ years) stems from several compelling reasons:

- Deporting undocumented migrants will cost billions, a significant financial burden on the UK economy.

- Past research has found that an amnesty has the potential to bring billions into the UK economy.

- Undocumented migrants are only able to regularise their residence after 20 years, leaving them at risk of exploitation and modern slavery.

Fund free eye tests and prescription lenses for everyone, I’d like the Government to help those whose eyesight means they spend hundreds of pounds a year on glasses to enable them to see. This is a commodity that most people get for free. We want the Government to fund regular eye tests and free prescription lenses for everyone., I cannot do anything without glasses (I have a prescription of -7.75). This is the case for many people, who spend hundreds of pounds every time our prescription changes, which can be frequently. I believe this is unfair. Given my family history I also expect to be paying out for my children to have tests and I think that sight should be a right to everyone and should not put strain on people financially.

Give victims of crime the right to appeal court decisions, We want the Government to give victims the right to appeal any court decisions, including judgements and sentences. Currently victims are very restricted in their options to challenge court decisions, whereas convicts have greater rights to appeal judgements and sentences., We believe the current system is hugely frustrating for victims, and this can have a significant impact on their wellbeing.
 
Victims should be able to have their voices heard, and new rights to appeal court decisions would help achieve this.

Increase funding for NHS gender dysphoria diagnosis and treatment, The Government should provide more funding to the NHS to reduce the waiting lists for gender dysphoria diagnosis and treatment., I am writing a petition to the Government to raise awareness about the long waiting lists for gender dysphoria diagnosis, and transgender health services, in the NHS.
 
By doing so, I hope to put pressure on the Government to provide more funding to the NHS to reduce these waiting lists. This would benefit people who have gender dysphoria by providing them with more timely access to diagnosis and treatment, which can improve their mental health and overall well-being.

Add a Bank Holiday commemorating the Windrush Generation, We want the Government to make 22nd June a bank holiday to commemorate the Windrush Generation. The Windrush generation have made an extraordinary contribution to British culture and our lives, greatly helping grow various staples in UK society, such as the NHS and TfL., Members of the Windrush generation have endured discrimination, prejudice and racism since they stepped off of the ship 75 years ago on 22nd June 1948.
 
It is especially important now to commemorate the achievements of this generation, given the recent Windrush scandal, that showed unacceptable hostility towards these people. It truly is the least we can do.

Require education on Gender Dysphoria in schools and workplaces, Gender Dysphoria should be explained properly in all schools and workplaces to stop the current confusion and the spreading of misinformation. Gender Dysphoria is not a choice, it has lifelong effects and many people do not understand the condition., The poor understanding of Gender Dysphoria leads to history repeating itself, segregation, discrimination, hate crimes as well as impacts on mental health and lack of medical help.
 
Our society in the UK is in a dangerous place, if things don't change now, we fear people with Gender Dysphoria will face the worst societal backlash since racism in the 1950s.
 
Requiring students be taught about Gender Dysphoria in school, and employees receive training on Gender Dysphoria at work, could help prevent this.

Fund year-round holiday activities for children with SEND and complex needs, Families in the UK are desperate for  provision over the school holidays for their SEND children. Government needs to provide meaningful support to these children throughout the year, equivalent to what is specified in the Holiday & Activities Fund provision for low income families., There is a gaping hole of extracurricular provision for SEND children in the UK, whether or not they are in receipt of free school meals. Short Breaks services continue to share HAF lists with users despite this mainstream provision being inaccessible to SEND children. 

For SEND children - who also benefit from year-round enrichment and socialisation -  Short Breaks direct payments are wholly inadequate, because there are so few activities that these children can access in the holidays.

Cancel the BBC license fee and shut down the BBC, The government should abolish the BBC license fee and the BBC itself, because the broadcaster does not represent the people, and because of scandals involving BBC staff., Especially as it is the only broadcaster with a licensing fee. If a broadcaster does not represent the people then should it not be closed down permanently?

Reform Hackney & Private Hire Regulations & Make It Universal, At present cross border is permitted, but cross council checks aren't. Opening up a difficult process when challenging illegal taxis. Liveries/plates are not universal, I believe there should be a universal approach such as having blue license plates for ALL taxis (example: Spain)., Having a universal approach to our taxi industry reduces the chance of illegal plying. By allowing all councils to have powers to check and penalise drivers from other councils would eliminate the time consuming process and close any loopholes that allow those drivers to continue working without any deterrent or consequence of their actions. Public welfare and safety is the forefront of our taxi industry and must be taken seriously. At present this is not the case and needs serious reform.

Ban sale of all sharply pointed kitchen knives, We call on the Government to introduce legislation to prohibit the sale of sharply pointed kitchen knives., As knives are the most common method of killing in homicides, reducing the capability of knives to cause penetrating injuries could decrease both homicides and other serious injuries.
 
The most common method of killing in homicides is a sharp instrument, including knives.
 
Additionally, research from De Montfort University looked at different types of knives and found that rounded-tipped knives do not easily penetrate clothing.
 
The use of rounded-tipped knives in household settings will also not significantly impact its utility. A knife’s blade fulfils most of the knife’s functionality.

Increase funding for NHS diagnosis of additional needs in children, The Government should provide more funding to the NHS to reduce the waiting lists for the diagnosis of additional needs in children by clinical psychologists., There is inconsistency of diagnosis waiting times depending on where you live. Some children wait months but others wait multiple years to be seen.

Stop the wearing of balaclavas, A lot of teenagers causing trouble, stealing from people at knife point and all seem to be covering faces with balaclavas so cannot be identified. Make it an offence to be caught wearing these to deter them from committing crimes as they will be recognisable,

Introduce AI fact checking for statements made by MPs in Parliament, Introduce Artificial Intelligence to fact check statements made by MPs in the House of Commons in as close to real time as possible., To help ensure that debates held in the Commons are based on real facts. This should be in real time, to reduce the need for potentially inaccurate statements to be investigated after the event.

Suspend UK membership of CPTPP pending a free and fair UK public vote, When we first joined the EC, a public vote had to be held and passed with a 50% vote in favour of membership. It is only right and fair that UK membership of the CPTPP is suspended pending satisfaction of the same democratic procedure., Because when we joined the EU, a public vote had to be held and won, so it is only fair and correct that the same procedure happens with UK CPTPP membership.

Normalise hormonal blood tests so female reproductive issues can be diagnosed., Women with menstrual issues are often not diagnosed properly and are put on the pill without thorough evaluation. Accurate hormonal blood tests are crucial for a correct diagnosis and personalised treatment to address their specific hormonal imbalance or disorder, preventing further complications., Normalising hormonal blood testing is crucial for women with menstrual issues who are fed up with being fobbed off when seeking help. Many have experienced frustration and dismissal, leading to misdiagnosis and ineffective treatments like unnecessary reliance on birth control pills. Accurate diagnoses will lead to personalised treatments, enhancing overall well-being and reshaping women's healthcare for the better.

Require third-party payment service checks for payments from trusts and estate, To check payments from trusts and estates are paid to the correct persons and beneficiaries.
 
To help prevent fraud, money laundering and financially motivated murders, and protect investors.
, A third-party payment service could be accessed via a worldwide portal of trusted professionals who are paid a small fee for their time and work checking the payments are lawful and correct.

Fund 35% pay rise for NHS staff, We want the Government to fund a 35% pay rise for NHS staff. We believe this is only fair during the cost of living crisis, especially when it is projected that the Sovereign Grant for the Royal Family is expected to increase by 45% by 2025.,

Increase funding for childcare for working parents of a child with SEND, Help working parents who have a child with special educational needs or a disability (SEND) access work by providing more funding for childcare. Accessing wraparound care and holiday activities for children with SEND can be difficult and costly, making it difficult for working parents., I want the Government to do this to help working parents, especially those who are unable to claim Universal Credit and claim 85% of childcare costs back. It should also help the country as a whole by helping those with children with SEND get into and stay in work, pay taxes and make a contribution.
 
Currently, I do not believe the system adequately supports working parents with children with SEND. I believe there is a serious lack of support.

Commission a cost/benefit study on joining the EU Single Market/Customs Union, Commission a study so the Government and people of the UK can see whether joining the European Single Market and Customs Union makes economic sense., Brexit, among other things, has damaged the UK economy and the Government needs to explore ways of reversing that damage. Without a proper study the Government cannot be fully informed and may be missing a solution to our economic problems

Fund the provision of smaller schools for those with complex SEND , The Government should fund the provision of small local schools for children with complex special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) so that they don't have to be sent far away from their families., Children with complex needs can be sent more than 2 hours away because of a lack of local schools for these children. This is not fair. These children need to be by their families and have a right to stay local just as much a mainstream school children.

Give us referendum over net-zero!, We the people want a referendum over all and every policy of net zero!, The public have lost faith in the government, a huge storm is brewing and its a salient fact that can't be ignored, the government is meant to serve and the public at large feel they are showing that they think they rule, its not acceptable in a democracy. Restore faith now and let us choose. The Uk is in turmoil because of government over reach, We don't want to suffer because you signed up to deals that we don't want and without our consent. Its dictatorial and unfair, do the right thing!

Amend the British Museum Act to allow the acceptance of repatriation requests., Some artefacts exhibited or kept in the British Museum for hundreds of year, should now be returned to their countries of origin.

Amend this piece of legislation to at least give the British Museum trustees the freedom to accept repatriation requests and enter into negotiation for their return., The removal of these artefacts from their countries of origin have been contentious ever since they were removed, such as the the 'Parthenon Marbles', The 'Benin Bronzes' and the 'Rosetta stone'. These Artefacts represent part of the history and cultural identity of millions of people.  After exhibiting them in the British Museum for hundreds of years, it is time to discuss the return of these artefacts to their rightful owners.

Celebrate and support disability pride month, We want the Government to celebrate and support disability pride month in July, in the same way it supports pride month for the LGBT+ community in June., As a disability advocate I think it is important to celebrate everyone and I mean everyone! People with disabilities are too often made to be ashamed of themselves! That needs to change!
 
The Government is active around pride month for the LGBT+ community, but not disability pride month. I want to Government to celebrate and support disability pride in the UK, in the same way it does pride month for the LGBT+ community.

Get Essential Tremor recognised as a disability, Essential Tremor (ET) affects the nervous system and causes involuntary and rhythmic shaking in the knees, head, voice and most commonly, in the hands., The simplest daily tasks are a challenge such as using cutlery, drinking, writing, tying shoes and many other tasks. ET is a incurable and debilitating illness that worsens with age. It can also take a toll on people's work life if they have the condition.
 
We want the Government to get Essential Tremor recognised as a disability so that people with ET are protected under the Equality Act 2010. We believe this will ensure doctors take ET more seriously and provide better care and treatment for their patients with the condition. We think this will also help to prevent discrimination against people with the condition.

Legalise euthanasia, Make it legal for people to be euthanised if they want to, for instance if they have a terminal illness, disease or meet a specific criteria to be allowed to end their life., We think people are left to suffer from illness/disease. They live in unbearable conditions mentally and physically until their body stops functioning. Individuals should have the option to end their own suffering. If you are given a diagnosis and expect to spend years with physical changes and disabilities, you might be constantly thinking about your death until you pass away. If euthanasia was available, we think people could enjoy what is left of their life, knowing they won't be in agony for years after.

Reform parliamentary privilege to remove protection for defamatory statements, Enact primary legislation to reform the outdated and often misused and abused concept of parliamentary privilege, ending legal protection for defamatory statements made in Parliament., Reforming parliamentary privilege in this way would promote greater transparency, accountability, and equality under the law. By removing the legal immunity granted to parliamentarians for their statements within Parliament, all citizens would be held to the same standards, fostering a more just democratic system. This change would discourage misuse of privilege, prevent the shield of immunity from being exploited for low political gain, and enhance trust in the legislative process.

Require local authorities better protect victims of anti-social neighbours, We want the Government to require local authorities to ensure that they do not house individuals who have previously been anti-social neighbours from being housed next to tenants who have previously reported anti-social neighbours, and the local authority found those reports to be accurate., Anti-social behaviour can ruin people's lives and make home life unbearable, as there is little residents can do about this, especially if the properties are attached. Some victims of anti-social behaviour find it difficult to function or concentrate on their lives in a healthy way as they are consumed by the disruption at home. This can lead to them avoiding their home, experiencing anxiety and depression, and can even lead to homelessness. When someone has been identified as a victim of anti-social behaviour, local authorities should be required to ensure that they do not house individuals who have previously been anti-social neighbours next to them. Prolonged exposure to anti-social behaviour should not be allowed.

Change the waiting time for Diagnosis for ADHD and AUTISM, Cut the waiting times for Diagnosis for ADHD AUTISM, The risk to life 
Quality of life 
Making it easier for Diagnosis to get treatment .

The Govt to make it illegal to assist any migrant that try to enter Uk illegally, We want the Govt to make it illegal for any UK organisation to assist any migrant that tries to enter the UK illegally where the migrant has not yet reached the shore. Where the assistance is required in our territorial waters then only the Coastguard can provide the assistance., The general public are fed up with seeing illegal migrants being assisted by the coast guard and RNLI wasting tax payers money and the donations to RNLI from the public.

Create a specific offence of 'virtual mobbing', Whilst inappropriate social media communications may be caught by current legislation, virtual mobbing - including on social media - has not been specifically prohibited in the UK. We want a statutory offence to be created, prohibiting virtual mobbing in the UK., It has become too easy for a mob of users on social media to attack someone, and we believe current offences don't adequately cover this behaviour. We think a new offence is needed to reflect the impact this behaviour can have on an individuals' mental health.

Reduce school summer holidays to four weeks, Most schools have summer holidays for six weeks. We want the Government to require schools to shorten the summer holiday to four weeks. If desired other holidays could be made longer to make up for this., We believe summer holidays are too long, and that four weeks off would be plenty. Many parents struggle to arrange childcare or other activities over the summer holidays, and we believe six weeks is too long for children to go without the routine and structure of school.

Ban school uniforms in the uk, I would like for the Government to ban school uniforms across the whole uk because i believe it would make students happier and help with increasing behaviour and understanding in school., The reason for this is because most counties around the world especially Europe allow students to go to school in their own clothes. 
It would make students feel more free in their own clothes and more comfortable. I also believe that the intelligence of students would increase and bad behaviour would decrease especially in the summer because why would you wanna be stuck in hot and sweaty uniform. Obviously have some dress coding in the summer but i really think it would help with mental health.

Review Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), Around 1 in 4 children have a suspected mental health issue and there is not enough support for these children. Many young people are waiting months to access Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS). We want the Government to review CAMHS and consider how these services can be improved., It is vital that children and young people get the support they deserve and so desperately need.

Create a half penny (£0.005) coin, We want the Government to direct the Royal Mint to create a half penny coin, worth 1/200th of a pound., This would allow for the price of products to be changed more incrementally. For example, something could cost 94 1/2p rather than 95p.
 
Manufacturing the half penny would also help the copper mining industry, and be of interest to coin collectors.

Increase penalties for road traffic offences, There are too many death and injuries on motorways and other roads. We want the Government to increase fines, driving bans and custodial sentences for all road traffic offences. This should help deter dangerous driving., We think current punishments aren't severe enough so bad drivers do not learn. We need to see dangerous drivers punished appropriately to make roads safer for all.

Hold a statutory public inquiry into Gender Identity Ideology and Queer Theory, We want the Government to hold a Statutory Public Inquiry into the extent to which Gender Identity Ideology and Queer Theory have become prevalent in public services, and the impacts. We believe Education, the NHS, and the broader public realm have been cognitively captured resulting in harm., We consider Gender Identity Ideology to be a set of beliefs that includes the idea that people can have a gender that is different from their sex. Queer Theory is a perspective that challenges traditional assumptions about gender and sexuality. We see this as ideological groupthink that has become orthodoxy causing people to lose jobs, some children to have irreversible medical treatment, and women’s rights to be subverted. We are concerned Standards in Public Life seem to have been by-passed.

Extend gambling regulation to cover free online competitions, People can become addicted to online draws and competitions on social media and they may not have any support available. These draws and competitions should be regulated by the Gambling Commission accordingly., We want free online competitions, such as those on social media, to be subject to stricter rules, so require the Gambling Commission to regulate them.

Prohibit promotion of homosexuality/gender incongruence in schools & councils, The Government should introduce laws to prohibit the promotion of homosexuality and gender incongruence in schools and councils. There are concerns amongst some parents about the teaching of LGBT issues., In 2003, Section 28 of the Local Government Act 1988 was repealed. The provision was designed to prevent the promotion of homosexuality in schools and local authorities. 
 
Legislation could allow legitimate discussion regarding homosexuality or gender, but prohibit the promotion of such.

Identify common needs in EHCPs and require schools to support these by default, There has been a significant rise in the use of Education, Health and Care plans (EHCPs), with autism being named as the most common condition. I want government to analyse common requirements in EHCPs and ensure that schools implement these provisions by default. , All schools should provide staff with up to date special educational needs and disability (SEND) and autism training, to naturally meet these needs.
 
The government want to cut the number of EHCPs by 20%. Local authorities are struggling with the volume of EHCPs due to budgets, staffing and resourcing of the provision that is legally required in section F. Identifying common needs and implementing them as default practice (for example, sensory/movement breaks and staff trained in SEND conditions), should naturally reduce the need for EHCPs as children will be supported at SEN Support level. Inclusion and access to a quality education is a right for all.

Increase penalties for, and improve policing of littering., I propose that an increasing level of deterring fines be used, for example, £1000 for a first offence, £5000 for a second, and £10,000 for a third and subsequent offence. In this way, fines would be a real deterrent for people on most income levels. Enforced community service should also be used., Littering is a major problem for all sorts of reasons. It can cause injury and death to wildlife, cause toxic chemicals to enter the food chain via the soil, and have an adverse effect on peoples’ enjoyment of the area in which they live or visit.
Local authorities can not afford to spend time and resources tackling the issue, so a real deterrent must be put in place, which should be policed using every possible method. In this day and age of CCTV and mobile phone footage, along with the more conventional methods of policing, there really is no excuse for not being able to enforce a proper anti littering policy.

Support the community of Tottenham at Tottenham Cemetery., Support the community of Tottenham in oposing the future removal of grave items permanently from our loved ones graves (being limited to 1 per grave) and oposing only being able to decorate a small section of the plot rather than the full plot., we believe this is unfair to families & friends of those buried in TC to have to permanently remove items that have been thoughtfully chosen & placed on graves & only being able to have 1 item in future. Also that we should be able to decorate our loved ones full graves rather than just the area that is head stone size. We are happy to remove them, temporarily, for works to be carried out but want to replace the items after and demand an explanation as to why we can't replace them after.

Authorities /media must not generalize the public to support their statements., Generalizing and categorizing the public to support official statements without their consent is unlawful and can lead to unjustified regulations.Therefore, such actions must be banned. Anyone who publicly quotes someone's support must provide the number of supporters, the community, or individuals., Media and authorities often claiming to speak for all people in general. I have raised concerns about how adjustments to official laws and legislations are often based on generalized statements such as "people demand" or "65% of people (from?)," or  "I am the voice of mothers, women, etc."These false statements have led to the establishment of unjustified regulations.These statements must be justified with transparent evidence on whose behalf the statement is made, much like in a court of law.

Make bullying a specific criminal offence, We want the Government to make bullying a specific criminal offence. Bullying can have a devastating impact on the lives of victims., We believe bullying should be made a specific criminal offence, to recognise the seriousness of this behaviour, and the impact it can have. It’s time we wake up and fight against this evil.

Fund an autism awareness campaign, The Government should fund an awareness campaign to help people understand autism. In particular it should help people understand how to better approach people with autism and cope/ spread awareness of their mannerisms and how they express their emotions., Because I personally have autism and I struggle to express my emotions properly. As a result, it has caused arguments and I don't feel it’s right that me or anyone else with autism should be made to feel bad for something they can't control.”

Remove the requirement of "reasonable grounds" for stop and search, Currently the ability for police to use stop and search powers without reasonable grounds can only be used in anticipation of, or following an incident involving serious violence, for up to 24 hours under section 60 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act., A section 60 is only put into action after an incident. Section 60 should be permanent, 24 hours a day 7 days a week, giving the police powers to stop and search whenever they see fit. Hopefully this will lower the amount of people carrying a knife/bladed article.
 
With the number of families who are living without loved ones due to knife crime and an increase in the amount of knife crimes across the UK something needs to be done. Police can only act on a section 60 for 24/48 hours after an incident, this needs to be permanent to give them more power to stop and search. We need to keep the public safe and I believe this will help.

carrying a knife  should serve a minimum mandatory sentence of 5 years, Change the laws and sentencing on knife crime it's as dangerous as a firearm and is causing as many deaths it should be held the same, Our children are dyeing our children are killing every day another young child has been fatally stabbed or stabbed even a kitchen knife can do incredible damage if it carries the same charge as a firearm children might think twice about carrying and you save 2 lives 1 from death and 1 from a life in prison

Fund additional support for children who may have SEND, We want the Government to fund additional support for families with children who may have special educational needs or disabilities (SEND), and are waiting for or going through an assessment process., Families whose children are being assessed for, or awaiting assessment for, special educational needs or disabilities (SEND), can miss out on vital support for their child. We believe these children are being failed, and that more support is needed, so that children don't miss out while they are waiting to be assessed.

Hold a public awareness campaign to raise awareness of early menopause, We want the Government to hold a public awareness campaign to raise awareness of Early Menopause and the causes such as surgery, cancer treatments and certain health conditions. Early menopause can have a devastating impact on a women's physical and mental health., An early menopause can have a devastating impact on a women's life and her fertility. The symptoms associated with early menopause can lead to challenges which can go unrecognised in a younger population. The physical and mental impact of this can effect relationships and an individual's self-worth. Fertility struggles can compound this even further. There is a lot of stigma surrounding these issues, by raising awareness we can educate people, break down stigma and encourage support for these women.

Hold a public awareness campaign on seat belt requirements for children, Current seat belt laws for children are not sufficiently well understood, especially when it comes to children on school transport. The Government should run a public awareness campaign to make it clear that children on school transport should be wearing seat belts, where these are provided., There have been tragic incidents involving children not wearing seat belts on school transport. The law says that children should be in the correct car seat or wear seat belts where they are provided, but many do not, and too many drivers don't appear to be taking responsibility for this.

Protect Trans People’s Right to Treatment on Gender-Appropriate NHS Wards, The Health Secretary announced plans to ban trans people from medical treatment by the NHS on women- and men-only hospital wards in England. We believe this is unreasonable, dangerous and illegal and, whatever their own views, the Government cannot and must not allow it to go ahead., We believe this ban would violate the section of the Equality Act of 2010 which protects trans people from discrimination, and could endanger trans health and trans lives.
 
The Health Secretary has declared that this measure is for "the protection of women and future generations", when we fear it will actively exclude certain women and members of future generations. We believe this proposal is both unethical and inhumane, and will put the health of people living in England at risk.

Require all MPs and ministers to take equality and diversity training, Following the Conservative Party Conference where the Prime Minister made comments that we believe are insulting to transgender people, we want MPs and ministers to be required to complete equality and diversity training to try and ensure they don't insult people!, At the Conservative Party Conference on Wednesday 4th October the Prime Minister said "We shouldn't get bullied into believing that people can be any sex they want to be, they can't. A man is a man and a woman is a woman, that is just common sense."
 
We believe this statement will be hugely insulting and hurtful to many people, including the 262,000 people in the UK who have said that the gender they identify with is not the same as their sex registered at birth.
 
MPs and ministers should represent all people!

Give the Speaker the power to recall the House of Commons as they see fit, To enable proper parliamentary discussion and support parliamentary sovereignty, the Speaker of the House of Commons should have the powers to recall Parliament as they see fit, Currently the House of Commons can only be recalled at the request of the Government. We want this to change, so the Speaker can recall the House on their own initiative
 
This should help ensure policy is properly discussed first in the House, and prevent scrutiny of announcements made outside of the House.
 
We believe that this would help restore faith that proper representation is still a desire of all parties, and support public confidence in our system of government.

Compensate those affected by preparations for HS2 from Birmingham Manchester, Many have been forced to sell or close their homes, businesses, farms and land to make way for the planned HS2.
