These people should be assessed and compensated for the hardship, trauma and financial difficulty caused by the project, now that it has been cancelled., The lives affected by HS2 have been countless and now that it has been cancelled, many people are left heartbroken by what they have had to give up. Some have had to move away from or uproot family, some have been unable to afford a new life with the money paid, this list is far from exhaustive. The losses may never be fully recovered, but compensation may go some way to repairing the damage caused and the unnecessary stress.

Fund free counselling for victims of child abuse, We want the Government to fund free counselling for victims of child, because child abuse has been found to increase the likelihood of victims going on to engage in criminal behaviour. Free counselling for victims of abuse could help prevent this.,

Hold a referendum on the UK's membership of the World Health Organization, In the interest of democracy, fairness, equality, equity and rule of law we the people want the Government to hold a public referendum on the UK's continued membership of the World Health Organization. A leaflet providing full, transparent & honest information should be provided to all voters., In the past the people were not consulted and their consent not gained for the UK's membership of the World Health Organization. We believe this is an error that requires correction. We believe the W.H.O is unaccountable and does not represent the people of Great Britain, and are concerned that UK's continued membership will allow outside forces to dictate or direct decisions regarding the health of the people, including the actions to take in a "pandemic" situation.

Legalise Possessing Knives with a Licence, We believe legalising the possession of knives, with appropriate checks, could seriously reduce knife crime and deter those intending to use the for malicious intent., By implementing strict background checks, thorough licensing procedures, and mandatory training programs, the UK can ensure that individuals possessing knives are law-abiding citizens educated in responsible usage. 
 
Furthermore legalisation fosters a transparent environment, enabling law enforcement to focus resources on combating illegal activities. Public awareness campaigns following changes to the law could emphasise the legal, safe use of knives could help reshape attitudes and behaviours.

Send airplanes for the evacuation of British nationals stuck in Israel, The UK Government has refused support to its nationals, and to send government planes to evacuate people from Israel., The welfare and the protection of the life of our fellow compatriots should be of outmost importance. The UK government has again ignored the calls of its citizens for rescue, issuing only " vague statements" of support, as of recent.

Mandatory life sentences for involvement in trafficking women & children for sex, We ask the Government to take the lead in tackling human trafficking, in particular of women and children for sexual exploitation. We ask for the institution of mandatory life sentences for anyone involved in these crimes, to deter those operating at all levels of human trafficking networks., People continue to be trafficked globally, particularly women and children. Current measures are clearly not sufficient to tackle this heinous crime, which strips victims of their dignity and freedom. The institution and implementation of stricter, harsher punishments of the highest degree in the UK will act both as a warning and a deterrent to those involved at any level and should help to break the chain of trafficking taking place on our doorsteps.

Create a statutory offence of manslaughter by coercive or controlling behaviour, We want the Government to create a specific statutory offence of manslaughter by coercive or controlling behaviour. The legislation creating this offence should make it clear that it applies in cases where coercive or controlling behaviour cause someone to take their own life., Currently manslaughter is a common law offence. At present it does not appear to be common practice for a domestic abuser to be prosecuted for manslaughter when their victim takes their own life as a result of coercive or controlling behaviour; with many commentators arguing that this is due to evidential difficulties. 
 
Creating a specific statutory offence of manslaughter by coercive or controlling behaviour would give the Government and Parliament an opportunity to clearly define this specific offence in statute, and we would hope this would lead to more people being prosecuted for manslaughter in appropriate cases.

Stop charging extra for monthly direct debit or 6-monthly Car Road Tax, It is understandable that every driver has to pay car tax to drive on the UK roads. However, I don't think there is a need for the DVLA to charge extra if one decides to pay for six months tax instead of a full year, or pay it monthly by direct debit., If any paperwork is involved in the process then I think it is only fair for the DVLA to charge for the postage fee.

Prohibit cannibalism in the UK , Cannibalism has not been specifically prohibited in UK law. We want a statutory offence to be created, prohibiting cannibalism in the UK., Cannibalism is potentially dangerous and we believe is an unethical act that should be an offence even if the person whose flesh and/or body part and/or organ being eaten has consented. There should be a mandatory minimum sentence of five years in prison for committing the offence.

Seek to rejoin the EU Erasmus Scheme, Erasmus is a brilliant education scheme. It provided huge benefits for the young British people wanting to visit other European countries and learn about them, the cultures and meet people from European countries., I think it's a great shame that UK students have lost access to the scheme, and believe the Turing Scheme is an inadequate replacement.
 
Rejoining Erasmus would also mean EU residents could more easily visit the UK and learn more about our country and culture.

Commission an anthem for England for events such as sport, I would like the Government to commission an anthem to be used at events to celebrate and show respect to teams or individuals representing England, as opposed to the National Anthem dating back to 1745 which is about the King and not the country of England., The other nations of the United Kingdom have their own songs to celebrate their countries' achievements, and yet England uses the 'National' anthem which pertains to all of the UK and is directed to the King, not the country. Our Country is based on fairness, non-discrimination and equality. England should have its own anthem to be used to celebrate and show respect to teams or individuals representing England as do the other countries.

Replace the cap on bankers' bonuses., Large bonuses encourage short term investment decisions that can produce bad outcomes for the economy. Reckless behaviour should not be encouraged or rewarded.
Salaries were increased to compensate for lost bonuses, ensuring globally competitive remuneration without the need for bonus restoration., https://www.bbc.com/news/business-67264647

Require CCTV cameras on school transport for kids with special educational needs, Children with special educational needs are often transported to school via transport arranged through the council. We want cameras onboard to help ensure the safety of those onboard, and allow for the review of incidents involving students who may not be able to speak, report, or defend themselves., By requiring CCTV, whenever there is a situation in question - the footage can be reviewed so the situation can be better understood. Children with special educational needs may not report something inappropriate, or be able to explain their side of story, should an incident occur. Unfortunately some people are not always honest or kind, which can put children with special educational needs at risk.

Do not restrict the use of tents by homeless people, The usage of tents is not a lifestyle choice. It is an alternative for safety, including for when people are refused statutory care., When someone is forced to sleep rough they should be allowed to do it with privacy and dignity.
 
We are seeing a large rise in rough sleepers as a result of the cost of living crisis.
 
By restricting the use of tents the Government would be forcing people to sleep in worse conditions, potentially damaging their physical and mental health.
 
We believe that if it restricts the use of tents the Government will not see a resolution but higher exposure of rough sleepers on the streets.

Create a Sikh regiment in the British army, Thousands of Sikhs fought for Britain in the world wars, with many men being awarded the Victoria cross for their bravery. The British army quite rightly recognizes Nepalese (Gurkhas) soldiers and we believe it is only right the sacrifice of the Sikhs is honoured by forming a Sikh regiment.,

Raise awareness of discrimination against those of all faiths & investigate, November is Islamophobia awareness month. However I am of Indian Hindu background. Why don't we have hinduphobia, sikhphobia, buddhistphobia christianphobia awareness months? This needs a parliamentary debate because it is sheer discrimination. It favours one faith over the others.,

Review how mental health cases that come through 999 are dealt with, There needs to be a full review to look at how mental health crises are dealt with by the emergency services and dispatchers through 999 calls. The review should look at how people are triaged; the options available to responders; and the training provided., We believe the way 999 calls relating to individuals handling mental health crises are handled and responded to can be inappropriate, and make the situation worse. A review should look at how these situations are dealt with at present, and identify ways of ensuring that these calls are responded to appropriately in the future. 

New laws and legislation need to be passed to enable a better person-centered approach for people contacting 999 in crisis.

Provide for resentencing for everyone serving an indeterminate prison sentence, We call upon the UK Government to recognize and safeguard the human rights of Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) inmates, by enabling them to be resentenced so indeterminate sentences can be replaced., The current system has led to prolonged detention beyond initial tariffs, subjecting individuals to what we regard as psychological torture and exacerbating mental health crises.

The IPP continues to cause severe mental degradation. We believe this constitutes a violation of their human rights.

We implore the Government to make provision for the review of all cases, in a way which acknowledges the toll inflicted by prolonged detention and ensures fair, humane, and rehabilitative sentences. Action is needed to end this nightmare, affording all the dignity and rights they deserve.

Invest £16 million into improving dementia diagnostics , Around 1 in 3 people living with dementia in England never receive a formal diagnosis. , We believe that with recent news of life-changing treatments such as Lecanemab and Donanemab potentially becoming available in the UK, thousands of people may be unable to access these drugs because of inadequate diagnoses.

Lumbar Punctures have been found to be a fast, accurate and cost-effective way to detect signs of dementia. A £16 million investment could boost the number of Lumbar Punctures from 2,000 a year to 20,000; helping the NHS pay for infrastructure, equipment and specialist training. The annual cost of social and informal care for those with dementia is estimated to be over £20 billion - and it is estimated around 1 in 4 hospital beds are occupied by a dementia patient, this investment into diagnostics could present a clear and long-term economic benefit.

Provide funding to reduce NHS waiting times for surgery for children, I think that the Government should provide ringfenced funding to the NHS to reduce waiting times for children who are waiting for surgery. , NHS waiting list are currently at a record high. I believe that children are waiting too long for their procedures, and I think that this is harmful to them.

Increase the sentence to ten years minimum if you are caught carrying a knife , I think that the minimum sentence for being found carrying a knife should be increased to ten years. , People are needlessly losing their lives as a result of knife crime. This is destroying families. I believe that having a minimum sentence of ten years could help reduce knife crime and the destruction it causes.

Increase Environment Agency funding to protect ancient woodlands, Give the Environment Agency greater funding in order to enable it to more promptly investigate and prosecute those who commercially benefit from the destruction and vandalism of ancient woodland, especially in areas listed as Sites of Special Scientific Interest. , Laws are in place but they need to be enforced, which we believe is not happening properly.

Require schools to teach students about knife crime as part of the curriculum, We want the Government to focus on educating young people of the dangers and consequences of carrying a knife, to help reduce the cases of knife crime all together. We want greater awareness of this issue., We want the Government to focus on this issue because we believe many people, especially young people, do not trust the authorities to protect them. We need to find a way to divert children away from knife crime. We believe improving education about knife crime could significantly alter the amount of knife crime cases, by raising awareness of the dangers and consequences of carrying a knife.

Review arrangements for the prescription of contraceptive pills, We want the Government to review arrangements for the prescription of contraceptive pills, with a view to improving patient safety. Currently patients can easily get repeat prescriptions without seeing their GP or having any health checks. This can mean risk factors are missed., My sister passed away in April 2020 from a blood clot which we believe was caused by the contraceptive pill. She had not had a check-up for the 18 months she had been on the combined pill. If she had received regular check-ups the clot could have been caught and she might still be here today. Her name is Riszka Szymkowska and she was 22 years old.

Rescind the new visa requirements announced., The new requirements will cause a rip in many families for one, as published by parliament on February 2023, and will harm any industry which relies on migrant workers. It will additionally harm international students, such as myself., The new salary requirements will cause a chain of events which will put already struggling systems through more difficult times. 

Personally, I have always aspired to write for British TV. I have saved up for years to come and study here, and I intend to put my degree into good use. But it will be exceptionally hard to find a TV writers job which will pay £38.700 per year, two years into the market. Many students will struggle the same way, and all aspects of British society will be affected.

Urge the UN to send a peacekeeping mission to Balochistan Pakistan, We are deeply concerned about the human rights of civilians in Balochistan. We believe that the gravity of the situation cannot be overstated and it is imperative that we take action., We believe that the deployment of a UN peacekeeping mission could significantly help in alleviating the current crisis. Their presence could not only deter violence but also ensure that the world is accurately informed about the ground realities in Balochistan.
 
We believe that the people of Balochistan are relying on the international community to stand with them in their fight for justice and peace.”

Take forward the Mental Health Bill to reform the Mental Health Act 1983, We want the Government to bring forward legislation to reform the Mental Health Act, which was promised in 2017 and 2019 manifestos but was not included in the recent King's Speech., We believe the Mental Health Act 1983 is dangerously outdated and makes it too easy for people to be detained, and treated against their will, and too difficult to be discharged.
 
Mental health affects 1 in 4 of us within the UK and every year tens of thousands of people are detained under the Mental Health Act, and BAME people have higher rates of detention than white people.
 
The Government has published a draft Bill that would make a number of amendments to the Mental Health Act 1983, including to raise the threshold for detention and have more regular reviews of detention, and give mental health patients great rights to make choices about the treatment they receive. We want this legislation to be taken forward.

Introduce a fast-track process for cases involving coercive control, Change the law so cases involving coercive control can be heard quickly. Waiting for these cases destroys people’s mental health and is extremely expensive., Cases should be heard quickly with short time frames for the respondent to build a case against the evidence, as they should have their response to hand. The process should allow an order to be drawn up very quickly. 

This way living arrangements can be sorted quickly, helping to avoid devastating impacts on children's upbringings and people’s mental health. It’s destroying lives.

Require LAs to reimburse education costs following tribunal/if they concede, The Government should introduce rules to require that a Local Authority (LA) must pay families back for the educational provisions they have self-funded, if those provisions were granted at tribunal or where the LA concede., Families of children with SEND whose needs are not being met are frequently self-funding hundreds/thousands of pounds in educational provisions while waiting for tribunal or before the LA concede and begin funding these educational provisions.

If LAs had to pay back families, this would also discourage refusals to fund specific provisions or placements for any other reason other than that they’re confident a suitable education is already being funded by the LA.

Hold a parliamentary vote on assisted dying, This petition calls for the Government to allocate Parliamentary time for assisted dying to be fully debated in the House of Commons and to give MPs a vote on the issue. Terminally ill people who are mentally sound and near the end of their lives should not suffer unbearably against their will., We believe dying people in the UK should have the option of requesting medical assistance to end their lives with dignity, through a safe and compassionate system with strict eligibility criteria and safeguards. Without this, too many are taking matters into their own hands with tragic consequences. The Daily Express and Dignity in Dying support Dame Esther Rantzen's call for a free vote. The time has come to Give Us Our Last Rights.

Increase the tax-free dividend allowance for stocks in UK businesses, We want the Government to increase the tax-free dividend allowance for stocks in UK businesses.
 
This should encourage investment in UK businesses, and increase individual motivation and ability to invest for their future, helping to reduce further burden on state pensions and welfare.
, I believe the reductions in the tax-free dividend allowance is further reducing the ability for the individual investor to provide financial security for their future and reduces the incentive to save/invest beyond the current allowance.
 
This should encourage increased investment in UK businesses, and help strengthen the UK as a services industry, and provide the UK stock market with the inflow it needs.

Make parents liable for any damages caused by minor children, In cases when minor children cause damage to private properties, for example due to anti-social behaviour, we want the parents of those children to be legally responsible for covering the costs of damages, such as repairs/replacements., Too many children cause damage to other properties, and a lot of parents don't take responsibility of the behaviour of their children. If parents had to cover the costs of any damages caused by their children, this could encourage parents to take more of an interest in what their kids are doing, and the need to raise them responsibly.

Enact stricter final effluent standards to protect water from pollutants, The Environment Agency does not require filtering out heavy metals, pharmaceuticals, disruptors, and microplastics in its final effluent standards. This can lead to ecological harm and public health risks., We want the Government to introduce stronger final discharge effluent standards for water companies in England that include these. 
 
We believe enhancing standards to include these is essential for environmental and community safety.
 
Current limits of 25 mg/l O2 for BOD and 125 mg/l O2 for COD fail to address key pollutants like heavy metals, pharmaceuticals, endocrine disruptors, and microplastics.
 
Without Government action, water companies are unlikely to act. We believe immediate action is essential to safeguard our waterways and public health and prevent an impending ecological crisis.
